q: Which sequence is the five-part pattern every good workflow follows?
options: Trigger, gather, process, output, human check
explanation: Every good workflow has the same skeleton: trigger → gather → process → output → human check. Only the last step belongs to you.

q: In a meeting follow-up workflow, notes are saved, AI extracts decisions and action items, and a draft email appears. Where is your checkpoint?
options: The trigger is missing, so the workflow will not run
Reading and correcting the draft before you hit send
The AI should send the email automatically
explanation: The human check is the final step — you review before anything goes anywhere important. It is not a weakness; it is the feature that lets a workflow run for months.

q: According to the lesson, where do workflows most often fail?
options: Inside the tool, because AI is too slow
On the drawing board — a trigger nobody set up, an input nobody feeds, an output nobody reads
Because the human check slows them down
Because free tiers cannot run workflows
explanation: Workflows fail on the drawing board, not in the tool. That is why you design the whole job on paper first — and keep the human checkpoint in every run.
